pr_body:
This PR integrates CCS with the new search_shards API. With this change, we will be able to skip shards on the coordinator on remote clusters using the timestamps stored in the cluster state.

Relates #94534
Closes #93730
pr_title: Integrate CCS with new search_shards API

review_comment: Do we need this because it is difficult to test directly against searchable snapshots, which is the only case where we rewrite on the coord node?

I find this test useful, at the same time I wish that we could split it and test different aspects separately. I wish that certain parts could be tested via unit test as well.

Some aspects that seem important to test (including those that relate to the previous PR around adding the search shards API):
- search shards excludes shards that cannot match based on metadata from the cluster state (frozen indices only)
-  search shards returns only shards that may match based on the can match executed on the data nodes
- shards that are returned don't execute can match once again as part of the can match for local shards, while we do execute can match for the other shards
- the number of skipped shards reflects the total number of skipped shards across all clusters

I believe an IT test here is more suitable because we are performing a real CCS search and assert our expectation. I've hardened this test (in https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/95894/commits/0409f7300bb774fb1cbe7dce452611e2d32161d0) to cover all the bullets.

Now that I see search shards being used, I am wondering why we need two flags in `SearchShardsResponse`. Intuitively, anything returned from that API is prefiltered by definition, and do we need the list of skipped shards or could we replace that with a counter? Maybe we need a third class for the bw compatibility layer that incorporates the SearchShardsGroup and tell where it comes from (old or new). It looks to me like serializing these flags over the wire is not necessary, is that the case?

I know this is controversial, but the BWC layer is very small. I opened https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/96123 to remove the `prefilter` flag. I will try to come up with an  alternative here.

@javanna I have pushed https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/95894/commits/8f5b715aaeac886f0d4f1551141ea5b0d067921b to handle the `preFiltered` flag. I think this approach is cleaner. WDYT? Thank you for pushing it.

minor nitpick:

The string `"cluster_a"` is repeated several times throughout the class. Would it be better to create a static final String called REMOTE_CLUSTER, so as to not repeat and also make code like this look more uniform:

```
for (String cluster : List.of(LOCAL_CLUSTER, REMOTE_CLUSTER)) {
```

instead of 

```
for (String cluster : List.of(LOCAL_CLUSTER, "cluster_a")) {
```
(optional)

A minor nice-to-have, but it would be good to move the javadoc from the other constructor down to this one and document the new parameters.

I had to go down to the "getter" methods for `skip` and `prefiltered` to understand what they represented.
